focus.jbig: October PPI at 8:30 ET · December hike near-certain · scanner boarded ZERO · stand down
focus.jtag: The October Producer Price Index lands pre-open into a tape already pricing a December Fed hike as near-certain. NVDA steadies ~+2% after Huang's resignation, oil eases, and the 10-year sits at 5.10%. The full-universe scanner ran and boarded no qualifying Type A, B or C setups
focus.jnote: The scanner did its job and found nothing — that is the signal. On Thursday the S&P 500 dropped 0.35% to end the day at 7,592.40, and the Nasdaq Composite shed 0.39% to 25,366.09. The CBOE Volatility Index increased 6.9% to 18.70. Overnight the tape steadied: futures on the Dow rose 0.2% while those on the S&P 500 gained 0.3%, and CFO Colette Kress stepped in as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor, with Nvidia shares rising about 2.67% premarket. The dominant event today is scheduled: the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the wholesale inflation data today, November 13, at 8:30 a.m. ET. Economists expect producer prices to increase 0.4% month over month in October, following September's unusually large 1.3% increase. Oil gave back some of Thursday's jump — WTI declined 0.25% to $88.52 a barrel. A scheduled CPI/PPI print inside 24h means a Sniper does not open new premium.
focus.notdown: Energy is the one group with a steady bid — the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) rose 1.5% on Thursday as Middle East supply and shipping risk lingered. But this remains a two-sided war-and-supply trade, not a clean Sniper: prices slipped Friday after Trump said a deal with Iran was not necessary to end the war, indicating he will stick with the blockade, and any de-escalation or surplus headline gaps crude back down. No energy name cleared the scanner. Watch-only.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive, high-multiple tech is the natural bearish lean into a hot-PPI/December-hike setup — a wholesale reading above 0.4% could boost bets on a half-point December hike and put pressure on tech stocks. But selling bear calls the morning of a scheduled inflation print, with NVDA squeezing +2% off its lows and the AI complex whippy, carries violent two-sided gap risk. The scanner confirmed it: zero Type A or B bearish names qualified. Sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Three things stack. One: a scheduled inflation print (October PPI) lands at 8:30 ET with VIX expanding — by the master rules that alone forbids GREEN. Two: P(≥1% gap) at ~37% is above the 35% trigger and composite 52 is WARM. Three, and most important for a Sniper: the full-universe scanner boarded ZERO names — no post-earnings gap, no news catalyst, no clean ATH breakout cleared the filters. There is simply nothing to take. Stand down on new credit spreads, let the PPI number clear, and re-run. Cash is a position today.

risks: October PPI · today 8:30 ET — a reading above 0.4% could boost bets on a half-point December hike and pressure tech, while a 0.2% or softer print could pull yields down and help gold toward $4,000. This is the number-one scheduled catalyst and the reason GREEN is locked out.

December Fed hike — size is the question — almost 88% of traders expect a 25-basis-point hike, and the rest expect a half-point move. Friday's PPI is the last CPI or PPI report before the Fed decides on December 9. A hot print shifts the whole curve.
10-year near 5.10% — Treasury yields hit 5.10% as oil rose and renewed inflation concerns pressured sentiment. A further rate pop compounds pressure on high-multiple tech and rate-sensitive groups.

NVDA leadership transition & earnings Tue 11/17 — Huang left after 33 years following reports of relationships including a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset, and CFO Colette Kress stepped in as interim CEO. The stock steadied premarket but the print next week is a live two-sided AI-complex catalyst.

Strait of Hormuz shipping — attacks on tankers transporting crude out of the Gulf and strikes on Saudi infrastructure by Houthis keep supply risk live even as oil eases. Any escalation sends crude and jet fuel vertical — the week's biggest geopolitical tail.
